policy.sources: A mark ships only when it was retrieved from the source recorded beside it and shipped byte for byte. Nothing here is redrawn, traced, recolored, or reconstructed from a screenshot. Three source kinds appear, and each record says which it is: a vendor's own host, fermix's checked-in plugin catalog, and fermix's own first-party artwork.
policy.no_fabrication: A vendor whose official mark could not be retrieved renders as the vendor text name beside a neutral SF Symbol. A monogram is never invented and another vendor's mark is never substituted.
policy.neutral_symbols: One neutral symbol per roster kind, so the fallback carries no invented vendor identity: providers use cpu, channels use bubble.left.and.bubble.right, meeting platforms use video, plugins and features use puzzlepiece.extension. All exist on the macOS 15 floor.
policy.accessibility: A mark is decorative at every site that draws one: the row around it carries the name, so nothing is spoken twice. The label recorded here is the name that row must speak, and it is unique within its kind. Two kinds may name one vendor, because Discord and Slack are each both a channel and a plugin.
policy.sizing: Marks ship as the vendor's own file, in the format that vendor serves, and the file is named for the format its bytes actually are. An SVG is resolution independent; a raster is at least 128 points on its shorter side, which covers the 20 to 36 point tiles at 2x. A vendor that publishes a horizontal lockup rather than a square icon is shipped as that lockup, because cropping one into a square is an edit no record here permits.
policy.origin: Every record names where its bytes came from, and the refresh step reads it: vendor marks are re-downloaded from the vendor's own URL, while catalog and first_party marks are pinned to fermix's own repository and are re-vendored there rather than fetched from a third party.
policy.plate: Every shipped mark records the plate it is drawn on, and the app reads that field rather than guessing from the pixels. neutral: a coloured glyph on transparency, inset on the app's own tile. bleed: the file is an opaque square or disc carrying its own ground, so it fills the tile and is clipped to its radius. There is deliberately no third plate: a plate painted under a single dark ink is the treatment GitHub and Notion were given on 2026-09-03, and it failed both ways, vanishing into the light ground it matched and glaring on the dark one. A vendor that publishes two inks resolves by appearance, and a vendor that publishes one that already carries its own light ink needs nothing. The catalog's brand_color is not used as a plate either: painting a vendor's brand colour behind a mark authored for white is a recolouring of the mark's context that no record here permits.

linux.scope: Each vendor record here is the macOS record, word for word, for a mark the Linux app draws. Asset paths are relative to app/marks/, which mirrors the macOS VendorMarks directory, and every file there is byte for byte the macOS file with the sha256 its record gives. A Linux-only fact about a record is in its linux_note field. The pet, wordmark, app_icon and app_icon_symbolic records are the Linux app's own; an asset path that leaves app/marks/ (../) names a file elsewhere in the workspace. roster_source describes the macOS ROSTER.json, which is not copied. app/src/marks.rs tests that its table, these records and these files agree.

omitted.computer_history: Linux has no Computer history row: the Integrations page's Features filter lists computer_use and meetings only.
omitted.computer_use_sidecar: Not a plugin row on Linux: plugins.list does not list it, and the Computer pane heads it with its own switch. Its file, features/computer-use-color.svg, ships for the computer_use feature.

linux.neutral_icons: The Linux fallback, one per kind: providers network-server-symbolic; channels fermix-chat-symbolic, the app's own speech bubble, because the GNOME 50 Adwaita theme has no plain chat bubble (it has no chat-bubbles-text-symbolic); meeting platforms camera-video-symbolic; plugins, features and sign-in clients application-x-addon-symbolic. It is drawn smaller than a mark and dimmed, so it never reads as one.
linux.decoding: An SVG is drawn by GTK's own SVG renderer (GtkSvg, GTK 4.22), which needs no image loader, so it also draws in the dev loop and stays sharp at any size. On 2026-09-25, at 128 pixels wide, it matched rsvg-convert 2.62.4 on every SVG here but two: no pixel differed by more than 10 percent, apart from 15 anti-aliased edge pixels of providers/openai-color.svg that differed by less than 25 percent. The two are channels/discord-blurple.svg and channels/discord-white.svg, which colour their path with a <style> element GtkSvg does not implement and so drew black. Where GtkSvg reports a feature it does not implement, the app decodes the file with the image loader (glycin), as GTK's own icon loader does. A raster (PNG, WebP) always goes to the image loader. The loader runs in the installed app, where every file here decoded on 2026-09-25; the dev loop runs the runtime directly, cannot start the loader's sandbox, and so decodes PNG only.
linux.plates: bleed fills the 32 pixel slot and is clipped to an 8 pixel radius; neutral is drawn as is in the slot. The app draws no tile under either.

marks.usage_terms: The official branding page states the marks may be used to inform people that you are a Discord user or have a Discord server, subject to the brand guidelines, and that you must not edit, change, distort, recolor, or reconfigure the Discord logo, or use the marks on merchandise. Published colors: Blurple #5865F2, Light Blurple #E0E3FF, Black #000000.
marks.permitted_treatment: Ship the vendor's own symbol files verbatim and scale uniformly. Never recolor: the black and white files are the vendor's variants, not tints of the blurple one.
marks.dark_mode_policy: Blurple is the default in both appearances. Where a surface needs a monochrome mark, light appearance takes discord-black and dark appearance takes discord-white, both official files.
marks.notes: The branding page's Color and White symbol download links are transposed relative to the archives they serve: the link labelled Color delivers Discord_Symbol_White and the link labelled White delivers Discord_Symbol_Color. Each asset here records the URL that actually contains its member, so the fetch script verifies content rather than the page's label.
marks.linux_note: GTK's own SVG renderer does not implement the <style> element that colours this path, so the app decodes discord-blurple.svg with the image loader instead, as GTK's icon loader does. It draws in the installed app; in the dev loop the loader cannot start and the row shows the neutral channel icon. The black and white files ship with the record and are not drawn, as on macOS.

marks.usage_terms: The brand kit page publishes the marks and the kit's own DESIGN.md carries the rules. On the files: "Always use these approved files. Never redraw, retype, or recreate any mark." On the keys, which is the mark used here: "The keys are the compact symbol for the brand. Use them cleanly and never decorate, outline, fade, or redraw the vector.", with "Do not change the opacity of the keys." and "Do not modify curves, anchor points, or proportions." On colour: "The logo only appears in Deep Blue, Off White, white, or black." and "For the logo: use Deep Blue on light backgrounds and Off White on dark backgrounds."

marks.usage_terms: Google's brand resource center routes logo use to its trademark guidelines at https://www.google.com/permissions/trademark/rules/, which state: “Use only Google-approved artwork when using Google’s logos.”, “Maintain clear space around Google logos according to the provided guidelines.”, “Don’t remove, distort, or alter any element of a Google Brand Feature.”, “Don’t display any Google Brand Features as the most prominent element in your content.” and “Don’t display Google Brand Features in any manner that implies a relationship with, affiliation with, sponsorship by, or endorsement by Google.” The brand resource center gates its own asset downloads behind an application (“Please complete your application to access brand resources.”), so what ships is the Google Meet product icon Google itself serves, byte for byte and unmodified.
marks.permitted_treatment: Ship the vendor's own file verbatim and scale uniformly. Never recolored, never cropped, never redrawn. It heads the Google Meet section of the Meetings pane beside that section's name, at the same measure every other mark in settings takes, so it is never the most prominent element on the page, and the copy around it names Google Meet only as a platform the notetaker joins.
marks.dark_mode_policy: One coloured camera glyph on transparency, which reads on both appearances, so it needs no appearance variant, is never rendered as a template image, and is drawn inset on the app's own neutral tile.
marks.notes: meet.google.com references this exact product logo path, which is how the current mark was identified: the older fonts.gstatic.com/s/i/productlogos/meet_2020q4 icon still resolves and is superseded artwork. The raster is taken rather than the 192 point SVG Google serves beside it, for the reason the Google sign-in client already records: AppKit loads that SVG but omits its feGaussianBlur filter, so the soft wedge inside the camera draws with a hard edge. The vendor's own raster renders the complete artwork with no custom renderer.

marks.usage_terms: This is the square application icon Zoom serves for its own site (the touch icon at https://www.zoom.com/apple-touch-icon.png), the current mark since Zoom's rebrand; written guidance is at “Zoom Brand Guidelines”, https://brand.zoom.com/. Zoom's own terms for the marks, published in plain text in its App Marketplace terms of service at https://www.zoom.com/en/trust/legal/zoom-api-license-and-tou/, state: “The “Zoom” word mark and the Zoom logo are trademarks and/or registered trademarks of Zoom (“Zoom Marks”). Subject to compliance with the Terms, Zoom grants SDK App developers a non-exclusive, non-transferable, royalty-free, fully paid-up, revocable, worldwide right and license, during the term of use of the Zoom SDK, to use the Zoom Marks solely for display within your SDK App and on your SDK App’s website to promote your SDK App’s compatibility with Zoom’s services and software. Zoom must agree in advance and in writing to all other uses of the Zoom Marks. All uses of the Zoom Marks must comply with Zoom’s Brand Guidelines and Partner Guide, which may be modified from time to time and are available at https://zoom.us/brandguidelines or from brand@zoom.us.” The Brand Center itself is a JavaScript portal: its logo library and the guideline text on it cannot be read without an interactive session, so the terms recorded here are the ones Zoom publishes as text.
marks.permitted_treatment: Ship the vendor's own file verbatim and scale uniformly. Never recolored, never cropped, never re-lettered, never redrawn. It heads the Zoom section of the Meetings pane beside that section's name, and the copy around it names Zoom only as a platform the notetaker joins, never as an endorsement or a partnership.

marks.notes: Zoom's Brand Center is an interactive portal, so the icon recorded here is the one Zoom serves for its own site chrome: 72 by 72 pixels, which covers the pane's 20 point tile at 2x. The media kit's downloadable file is a horizontal wordmark, which draws as a thin band in a square tile and is not used. marks.notes: The one record not shipped byte for byte: fifteen 1024 pixel layers decode to about 60 MB, and the mascot is drawn 108 points tall, 216 pixels at 2x, so each layer ships at 256 pixels. The command above is reproducible: run twice with this ImageMagick it gives the same bytes, which is what each sha256 pins, and source_sha256 pins the master it came from. Another ImageMagick version may resample differently, so a refresh re-records both. The masters are byte-identical from fermix commit 3dcce905, which added them, through fermix-macos commit 8852cc5, which added them at the path recorded here, to that repository's head on 2026-09-25. The pet is not a vendor mark and is drawn on no tile, so it has no plate. core/tests/mascot.rs fails when any layer is missing or is not a 256 pixel RGBA PNG.

marks.usage_terms: First party. MIT, copyright 2026 Tezra, per the fermix-macos LICENSE; the Linux workspace is MIT too.
marks.permitted_treatment: Shipped byte for byte and scaled uniformly. The letters are currentColor, so they take the text colour where they are drawn; the two eye-dots keep the file's own #2b5cff. Never redrawn, cropped, or recoloured in any other way.
marks.dark_mode_policy: One file in both appearances. macOS fills the letters with Palette.ink (#16161a light, #f4f5f7 dark) and the dots with Palette.accent (#2b5cff in both), in FermixWordmark.swift. The Linux app fills the letters with the text colour GTK gives the drawing, which follows light, dark and high contrast, and draws the dots as the file does.
marks.notes: The macOS file is the engine's fermix_wordmark/1 component saved as a file: the same viewBox, paths and dots as fermix apps/fermix_web/lib/fermix_web_web/components/core_components.ex, which has drawn it inline since fermix commit da36ce7c. fermix-macos added the file at commit 266f283 and it is unchanged to that repository's main, recorded above, on 2026-09-25. macOS draws a 1:1 path port of it (FermixWordmark.swift) because NSImage cannot tint a currentColor SVG, and ships the file as the reference the port is reviewed against; its welcome screen draws it 40 points tall.
marks.linux_note: app/src/wordmark.rs draws it at the head of the sidebar, 26 pixels tall with the file's own margin, so its letters stand 22 pixels tall. GTK's SVG renderer resolves currentColor to black, and a template fill would flatten the blue dots into the letters' colour, so the app sets the root element's color attribute to the text colour before GTK reads the file; the shipped bytes stay as recorded. GTK does not read the role and aria-label attributes, so the picture carries the accessible label Fermix itself.

marks.notes: macOS's one-ink mark: FermixMarkMaster.png, which scripts/build_mascot_mark.py derives from the pet artwork (the silhouette, the visor cut through it and the two eyes as ink inside it) and from which build_menu_bar_template.py rasterizes the menu bar templates. A GNOME symbolic icon is usually an SVG, but this mark exists only as a raster, and turning it into paths would be tracing, which this file's policy forbids; so it ships in GTK's raster symbolic format, name.symbolic.png, at the 16 to 64 pixel sizes symbolic icons are drawn at. At 16 pixels the eyes are about a pixel across and fade into the visor. macOS redraws them at a floor for its 18 point menu bar templates, which is a second drawing rule rather than a downscale, so it is not applied here.
marks.linux_note: Installed as /app/share/icons/hicolor/NxN/apps/io.tezra.Fermix-symbolic.symbolic.png. Checked on 2026-09-25 in the GNOME 50 runtime (GTK 4.22.5): the icon theme finds io.tezra.Fermix-symbolic at 16, 20 and 32 pixels, reports it symbolic and fills it with the colour it is given. Whether GNOME Shell's own icon loader reads a .symbolic.png was not checked.
